description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, crispy on the outside and tender inside, packed with fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. This classic dish is a delightful appetizer or a light meal, perfect for sharing with friends and family. Enjoy the authentic flavors of Korea right in your own kitchen with this easy-to-follow recipe.

instructions.title: Prepare the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, cornstarch, cold water, egg, and salt until a smooth batter forms. Ensure there are no lumps. Set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Clean and chop the mixed seafood into bite-sized pieces. Cut the green onions into 3-inch lengths and thinly slice the yellow onion. If using, thinly slice the red chili pepper.

instructions.title: Heat the Pan
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Ensure the pan is hot enough to create a crispy crust.

instructions.title: Assemble and Cook the Pancake
instructions.text: Pour about 1/3 to 1/2 of the batter into the hot pan, spreading it evenly to form a thin circle. Immediately arrange a portion of the seafood, green onions, and sliced yellow onion over the batter. Press gently to embed them into the batter. Cook for 4-5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy.

instructions.title: Flip and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Carefully drizzle another tablespoon of oil around the edges of the pancake. Using a large spatula, flip the pancake and cook for another 3-4 minutes until the other side is golden brown and the seafood is fully cooked. Repeat with remaining batter and ingredients to make more pancakes.

instructions.title: Make the Dipping Sauce and Serve
instructions.text: While the pancakes are cooking, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and toasted sesame seeds in a small bowl for the dipping sauce. Slice the cooked Haemul Pajeon into wedges, garnish with sliced red chili if desired, and serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

tips: Use cold water for the batter; it helps create a crispier pancake by inhibiting gluten development.
Dont overcrowd the pan. Cook one pancake at a time to ensure even cooking and maximum crispiness.
Press down on the pancake gently with your spatula while cooking to ensure good contact with the pan and a nice crust.
For an extra crispy texture, add a tablespoon of rice flour to your batter mix.
Serve immediately after cooking to enjoy the best texture. Pajeon is best fresh and hot.
article:
Haemul Pajeon: The Ultimate Guide to Korea's Crispy Seafood Pancake

Few dishes capture the heart and soul of Korean comfort food quite like Haemul Pajeon. This beloved savory pancake, bursting with fresh seafood and vibrant green onions, is a culinary masterpiece that tantalizes the taste buds with its unique blend of textures and flavors. Whether you're a seasoned K-food enthusiast or a curious newcomer, learning about and making Haemul Pajeon is an experience not to be missed. It’s more than just a dish; it’s a symbol of gathering, often enjoyed on a rainy day with a glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine), creating warm memories and satisfying cravings.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

At its core, Haemul Pajeon translates directly to "seafood green onion pancake." "Haemul" means seafood, and "Pajeon" refers to a pancake featuring green onions as a primary ingredient. Unlike its thinner, crispier cousin, the jeon (savory pancake), pajeon is typically thicker, often showcasing whole or large pieces of green onion embedded within a soft, chewy batter, crowned with an array of fresh seafood.

The magic of Haemul Pajeon lies in its contrasting textures: a beautifully crispy, golden-brown exterior gives way to a tender, slightly chewy interior, studded with succulent pieces of shrimp, squid, mussels, and other oceanic delights. The mild sweetness of the green onions complements the savory seafood perfectly, creating a harmonious flavor profile that is both comforting and incredibly satisfying. It's a versatile dish that can serve as an appetizer, a hearty snack, or even a light main course, universally loved for its deliciousness and easy shareability.

## Ingredients for Korean Seafood Pancake

Crafting an authentic Korean seafood pancake requires a thoughtful selection of fresh ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to gather for a truly memorable Haemul Pajeon:

*   **For the Batter:**
    *   1 ½ cups all-purpose flour (some recipes suggest adding a tablespoon of rice flour or cornstarch for extra crispiness)
    *   1 large egg
    *   1 ½ cups cold water or anchovy broth (broth adds depth of flavor)
    *   ½ teaspoon salt
*   **For the Fillings:**
    *   1 bunch (about 8-10 stalks) green onions, trimmed and cut into 3-4 inch lengths
    *   1 cup mixed seafood, fresh or frozen (shrimp, squid rings, mussels, oysters, clams – cleaned and chopped into bite-sized pieces if large)
    *   ½ small onion, thinly sliced
    *   ½ small carrot, julienned (optional, for color and sweetness)
    *   1-2 red or green chilies, thinly sliced (optional, for a hint of heat)
*   **For Frying:**
    *   4-5 tablespoons vegetable oil (or a neutral oil like canola)
*   **For the Dipping Sauce:**
    *   4 tablespoons soy sauce
    *   2 tablespoons rice vinegar
    *   1 teaspoon sesame oil
    *   1 teaspoon sesame seeds
    *   ½ teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)
    *   1 clove garlic, minced (optional)
    *   1 tablespoon finely chopped green onion

The quality of your seafood is paramount here. Fresh, high-quality shrimp, tender squid, and plump mussels will make all the difference in the final taste and texture of your Haemul Pajeon.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Haemul Pajeon

Making Haemul Pajeon is a fun and rewarding process. Follow these steps for a perfect pancake every time:

1.  **Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables:** If using frozen seafood, thaw it thoroughly and pat dry. Clean and chop all seafood into bite-sized pieces. Wash and trim the green onions, cutting them into 3-4 inch lengths. Thinly slice the onion, julienne the carrot, and slice the chilies if using.
2.  **Make the Batter:** In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, egg, salt, and cold water (or broth) until just combined. A few lumps are okay; overmixing can lead to a tough pancake. The batter should have the consistency of thin pancake batter, easily pourable but not watery.
3.  **Combine Ingredients (Optional Method):** Some prefer to mix the green onions and some seafood directly into the batter. For a more visually appealing pancake with distinct layers, you can arrange the green onions and seafood directly in the hot pan, then pour the batter over them.
4.  **Heat the Pan:** Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring it coats the bottom of the pan. The oil should be hot but not smoking.
5.  **Assemble and Cook the Pancake:**
    *   If using the layering method: Arrange a generous layer of green onion pieces in a single layer on the hot oiled pan. Scatter a handful of your mixed seafood, sliced onions, and carrots over the green onions.
    *   Pour about 1 to 1 ½ cups of batter evenly over the green onions and seafood, ensuring everything is coated. You might need to gently spread the batter with the back of a ladle to form a round pancake.
    *   Reduce heat to medium. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the edges are golden brown and crispy, and the bottom is firm. You can drizzle a little more oil around the edges to help with crisping.
6.  **Flip the Pancake:** This is the trickiest part! Carefully slide a large, thin spatula under the pancake. If it feels too fragile, you can place a large plate over the pancake, then carefully invert the pan onto the plate. Slide the pancake back into the pan, uncooked side down. Add another tablespoon or two of oil to the pan if needed.
7.  **Finish Cooking:** Cook for another 4-6 minutes on the second side, pressing down gently with your spatula to ensure even contact with the pan and encourage crispiness. The Haemul Pajeon should be golden brown and cooked through.
8.  **Repeat:** Slide the finished pancake onto a cutting board. Repeat with the remaining batter and fillings.

## Tips for the Perfect Crispy Pajeon

Achieving that irresistible crispy exterior while maintaining a tender interior is the hallmark of a great Haemul Pajeon. Here are some expert tips:

*   **Cold Batter:** Using cold water or broth for your batter helps prevent gluten development, resulting in a more tender pancake.
*   **Don't Overmix:** Mix the batter just until the ingredients are combined. Lumps are fine and contribute to a lighter texture.
*   **Hot Oil is Key:** Ensure your pan and oil are hot before adding the batter. This creates an instant sizzle, leading to a crispy crust.
*   **Enough Oil:** Don't skimp on the oil! It’s crucial for achieving that golden, crispy exterior. You can even drizzle more around the edges while cooking.
*   **Medium-High Heat:** Maintain a consistent medium-high heat. Too low, and the pancake will be soggy; too high, and it will burn before cooking through.
*   **Even Thickness:** Try to spread the batter to an even thickness in the pan for uniform cooking.
*   **Crispy Edges:** For extra crispy edges, gently press down on the pancake with your spatula during the last few minutes of cooking on each side.
*   **Ventilation:** Pajeon cooking can produce some smoke, so ensure good ventilation in your kitchen.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed fresh off the pan, while it's still warm and crispy. Cut it into wedge-shaped pieces or squares using a pizza cutter or knife.

The essential accompaniment is a tangy, savory dipping sauce. To make the classic dipping sauce, simply whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and optionally, gochugaru, minced garlic, and chopped green onion. This sauce cuts through the richness of the pancake and adds a delightful zing.

Traditionally, Haemul Pajeon is paired with makgeolli, a milky, slightly effervescent Korean rice wine. The combination is a match made in heaven, especially on a rainy day when the sound of sizzling pajeon is said to mimic the sound of falling rain. It also pairs wonderfully with soju or a cold beer, making it perfect for a casual get-together or as an appetizer for a larger Korean meal.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Haemul Pajeon is a masterpiece, there are many ways to customize your pajeon to suit your taste or available ingredients:

*   **Vegetarian Pajeon:** Easily omit the seafood and boost the vegetable content. Mushrooms (shiitake, oyster, enoki), zucchini, bell peppers, or even kimchi (for Kimchi Pajeon) make excellent additions.
*   **Meat Additions:** Some variations include thinly sliced beef (bulgogi-style) or pork belly for an even heartier pancake.
*   **Different Seafood:** Feel free to use your favorite seafood combination. Scallops, small fish fillets, or even imitation crab meat can be used.
*   **Spice It Up:** For those who love heat, increase the amount of fresh chilies or gochugaru in the batter or the dipping sauce.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Substitute all-purpose flour with a gluten-free flour blend, ensuring a similar consistency. You might need to adjust the liquid content slightly.

Haemul Pajeon is more than just a dish; it's a culinary experience that brings people together. Its irresistible crispy texture, savory seafood, and fragrant green onions make it a standout in Korean cuisine. With this guide, you’re ready to embark on your own delicious journey to mastering this iconic Korean seafood pancake. Enjoy the process, savor the flavors, and perhaps even create your own rainy-day tradition!
